about: KRW's 97 firms as a league table beside one of the two cards KRW published. The read-out gives M, the pairs the card states (N), their share s, the pairs that share a grade and the pairs inside each grade; the card legend gives the number of grades and the sizes; the details panel gives the selected firm (at a preset without a firm, the first row of the table's order). Card counts come from v1's frozen numbers registry (krw.*.card.N, .s, .sizes, .G) and the base-R oracle row disclosure-krw-sizes-2-81-14; the released values of the named firms (esttop, meantop, est2, statefarm) are registry keys too; the bar note's share is cf.normal.within1 and the interval levels are settings. The selected firm's pair line comes from the registry keys of the engine's unitRelationCounts and its base-R oracle rows. Literals: the KRW card caption (6.5), the headings and table caption (11.4), the grade-1 legend (3.3), the gloss (12.3), the race card's prior note, and the read-out (v1's three sentences, then one on how the card's directions run against the table's order) and the pairs lines word for word with their numbers as slots (9.4), at every preset. The read-out and pairs lines say how many of the card's directions run as the table orders them (its strictOrder ranks by estimate or by posterior mean) and how many the other way: race card 1,219 and 105 by estimate, all 1,324 by posterior mean; gender card 730 and 1 in both orders; Nationwide 15 and 1, State Farm 2 and 14 by estimate. These counts come from the engine's statedAgainst and match an R count with postrank 1.1.0's pr_case_krw; no golden or oracle row holds them yet, so they are checked as shown numbers (data-num read back) inside the word-for-word sentences. Pair counts inside the grades other than race grade 2 and gender grade 3 have no registry or oracle source and are checked only as shown numbers.

expect.about: under the race card: why every race interval lies right of zero (KRW's race prior; register CR-102)
expect.value: KRW's race prior puts all its weight on positive gaps, so every race posterior lies above zero, even for a firm with a negative estimate.
